Hooped firkins and hand-blown rose phials packed around a bell-jar of drifting luminous jellyfish-caps in deep gold suspension, one small corked bottle beside it holding bottled dawn, soft rose-light pooling at the base and brightening toward the stopper, each firkin ringed with violet-dyed thread, one phial frosted so cold it has glazed the plain shelf timber beneath it white.

Stoneware pots and beeswax tins crowded beside a tall phial where snowflakes spin in permanent slow fall and never once land, one sealed decanter holding a sea-storm in miniature, dark indigo water churning against curved amber glass, each tin left plain with no marking at all, one pot mended at its hairline crack with a seam of gold that catches every flicker of lamplight.

Birch-bark cylinders and stoppered gourds jostling hand-blown turquoise phials, one phial holding an hourglass-shaped inner vessel where glowing pollen-sand drifts upward in a slow golden column, one sealed emerald bottle where a tiny perfect tree has grown and turned every leaf to autumn fire, each gourd tied with a dried sprig tucked under brown twine, one bottle weighted under a flat river stone so it will not lift.

Corked green-glass bottles and stoppered gourds press three deep around a long-necked decanter whose deep ruby liquid pours perpetually upward, and a bell-jar holding a seedling that sprouts, flowers, and seeds again in a slow emerald loop, every gourd sealed in violet wax stamped with a painted crescent, one bottle so warm it stands in a saucer of water to keep its heat from the wood.
